#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9063bc30-b26a-4746-b0ab-25357a7e50ef/1d558aa9dd6599dfad2f4ae46a5f7bcff085d8bb__1_.png?t=1795701317)
Follow image link: (https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2125315491522650299?a=LrQR4cU_6WJdBWYtdrs&s=20)
Caption: Image Source: Anthropic

**Claude's **[**new desktop apps**](https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2125315491522650299?a=LrQR4cU_6WJdBWYtdrs&s=20)** are tiny, clever and not quite real**

If you've seen Anthropic's demo video floating around this week and wondered what the fuss is about, here's the simple version.

When Claude built you something before, say a tracker or a little dashboard, it lived in a browser tab. Now you can hit ["Install as app"](https://claude.com/resources/articles/install-as-app) and it [lands in your Dock or taskbar](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/24/anthropic-just-gave-claude-users-a-new-way-to-make-mac-apps/) with its own icon, like anything else you'd download. You don't write code or set anything up. If you want it changed, you just ask Claude and the app updates. It's in beta, and it's on [every plan](https://dev.to/vladimir_beskorovainyi/claudes-install-as-app-needs-you-online-i-built-an-open-version-that-doesnt-f5o), even the free one.

People are already having fun with it. Someone started a ["Claude AppStore"](https://github.com/fengyiqicoder/claude-appstore) list on GitHub, and it's got a shooter game, a geography quiz, a Mac cleaner and a planet you colonize over 60 years. Honestly, though, I think the best uses will be boring. A shop owner who gets a ping at 4 pm when an order hasn't gone out. A student with a countdown to every exam. Stuff no developer would ever bother building for you.

Here's the "not quite real" part. Someone pulled one of these apps apart and found it's [404 KB](https://github.com/fengyiqicoder/claude-appstore), basically two tiny files and an icon that open a window inside Claude. That's why it won't work offline, why you have to stay signed in, and why everything it does eats into your usage limit. Another person asked Claude for the same app two ways and got two very different things back: a proper app that works without Claude but never changes, and an installed one that keeps changing but can't exist without Claude.

The bit I'd actually be careful with is [permissions](https://thenextweb.com/news/claude-install-as-app-artifacts-mac-windows-desktop). An app can ask for full access to your computer, which means running programs and reading, changing or deleting your files without asking you first. You can only give that to apps you built yourself, and Claude checks with you again after every update. But nobody at Anthropic reviews these apps, and turning access off later [won't undo](https://i10x.ai/news/claude-artifacts-install-as-app-mac-windows-permissions) anything an app already did. So I'd only say yes for apps I made and understand.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Yoroll](https://code.yoroll.ai/?utm_source=ai_valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=black_friday_2026&utm_content=trending_tools_20261126) - turn an idea into a playable 3D game with Yoroll Code. Its team had a #1 product on Product Hunt ^~(sponsored)~^

* [Gemini 4 Neon](https://blog.google/intl/en-in/products/introducing-gemini-4-neon/) - mid-tier multimodal model for reasoning and agent tasks, with a 1M-token context window

* [Install as App](https://claude.com/resources/articles/install-as-app) - Claude beta feature that lets you install artifacts as standalone Mac and PC apps

* [Treg People API](https://x.com/treg_ai/status/2125546075855741424?a=syujNcuqTTiWUz9uCec&s=20) - API that looks up a person's identity details like phone number, personal email and social traces

* [MyClaw 3.0](https://myclaw.ai/) - build an always-on team of AI agents that share a common memory

* [MAGI-1](https://sand.ai/) - first autoregressive video model to deliver top-tier output quality

* [Perplexity Time Machine](https://x.com/perplexitydevs/status/2125676416834605488?a=65b11mttDKta5TRv3PA&s=20) - shows a model the web exactly as it looked on a date you choose

* [Ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama)** - **Runs large language models on your own machine. macOS, Windows, Linux, Docker, one-command setup

* [AutoGen](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen)** - **multi-agent framework: agents that talk to each other to solve a task, with customizable roles and proper docs


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------
* The CEO of Anthropic thinks chat is temporary and talks about [what the next interface](https://x.com/okkshitij/status/2125623846934127008?a=ILgAKO1fMISju_8kMPQ&s=20) should look like

* OpenAI and Anthropic are [done with AI](https://x.com/atmoio/status/2125595888160772119?a=ZjZfeMdOBYmUx-TVj8I&s=20)

* The [most badass PowerPoint ](https://claude.ai/artifact/Cy2d8Vn63CnzCtonA1LSah)ever, from Opus 5.6 with a single prompt (because the visuals are so elaborate, the original link takes a while to load)

* How to build your own Grok bot for free ([Hermes full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Y3H9agIcSQ))

* [Scaling swarms](https://x.com/lvwerra/status/2125612908499349833?a=3mchlX6kIz9apw9nsVk&s=20) to thousands of agents

* [My median predictions](https://x.com/danrobinson/status/2125699708559802741?a=q2OyPg7N4Nu5rbp3DT0&s=20) for RSI in 2027

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy tuesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Jensen is back. I was wrong

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **VIKTOR**

## [Your company knows more than anyone who works there](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main15-hl)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/34c80382-6d56-41de-b5d6-eaf5580be52d/viktor_main_ad_nov24_1280x720__1_.jpg?t=1795530592)
Caption: Courtesy: Viktor.com

Marketing knows which ad brought the lead. Sales knows the lead never bought. Finance knows what the ad cost. Nobody holds all three, so every decision runs on a slice.

Viktor is the AI employee who holds the whole picture. He works in Slack, Microsoft Teams and email, connects to 9,800+ tools, and remembers what each team tells him.

Ask him one question: "Which ads paid for themselves last month?" He reads the ad accounts, the CRM and the billing data, then hands back the audit as a PDF. Once you approve, he moves the budget to what works.

Companies that decide on all they know pull ahead of the ones that guess. 80,000+ teams have hired him. Your data never trains a model.

[Start free with up to $100 in credits.](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main15)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/caf8f11e-657c-41e6-a9fe-2ce613289ae6/Jensen_2.0__1_.png?t=1795528111)
Caption: Image Courtesy: GavinSBaker

**Jensen is **[**back**](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director)**. I was wrong.**

Last week I wrote that Jensen Huang wouldn't be back at Nvidia before the investigations finished, "however many people sign." Prediction markets agreed with me: Kalshi had his odds of returning at 9%.

On Monday, Nvidia's board [voted unanimously](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045810/000104581026000090/nov23pressrelease.htm) to bring him back. The investigations haven't finished. So that aged well.

What makes it stranger is that six days earlier, on the earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones said the board had no intention of reinstating him. Then the White House got involved. ["I made the deal,"](https://abcnews.com/Politics/made-deal-trump-convinced-nvidia-board-reinstate-jensen/story?id=138373104) Trump told CNBC. Semafor reported that he dialed into a board meeting himself, and CNN reported that JD Vance spent the weekend calling directors. The board now says senior government officials assured it that Huang's return poses no national security risk.

The market didn't care how it happened. Nvidia closed up 31.5%, adding [roughly $950 billion](https://edition.cnn.com/2026/11/23/business/live-news/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-ceo-of-nvidia) in one day, about double the previous record for any company.

Huang's first day back was oddly low-key. He [skipped the leather jacket](https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-war/article/3375539/jensen-huang-returns-nvidia-applause-staff-no-trademark-leather-jacket-sight) for a navy work jacket and sneakers, and reportedly [handed out](https://x.com/RT_com/status/2125033090028392465?a=8t8FDbp88H6wuRnX7fc&s=20) mini sandwiches from a paper bag. Employees lined three floors of railings chanting his name. He apologized for putting them through all of this, joked that he'd need to get a new computer from IT, and [promised](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/jensen-huang-returns-nvidia-headquarters-222816911.html) to be "a better CEO the second time around." Not everyone was cheering, though. Some employees reportedly called his return ["the worst outcome."](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/big-tech/jensen-huang-returns-to-applause-from-employees-at-nvidia-hq-some-employees-reportedly-disgruntled-by-return-saying-this-is-the-worst-outcome)

Washington is less moved. Lawmakers from both parties are angry, Megaspeed is now on a US trade blacklist, and Huang faces Congress on December 1 and 3. The board's own investigation is still running.

**My three earnings-day questions, scored:** the chip roadmap is on track (Vera Rubin brought in nearly $20 billion in its first quarter), China revenue is assumed to be zero, and the CEO search ended with the old CEO.

Here's what I keep coming back to. Nvidia lost about a quarter of its value when he left, and got most of it back the day he returned. That's not just a comeback story. It's a price tag on one person. Nvidia is probably better with him.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------

* [Inkling 2 Mini](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-mini/?utm_source=thedeepview&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=macbook-pro-s-real-upgrade-isn-t-the-touchscreen) - the newest model from Thinking Machines, compact enough to run locally on a laptop

newsletters.title: Your AI Agents Can Multitask. Can You?
newsletters.content:
Managing several agents means constant context switching. Here’s how nine people at Every handle it.  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

https://every.?ev_audience=free View in browser https://every.?ev_audience=free


YOUR AI AGENTS CAN MULTITASK. CAN YOU? https://every.?ev_audience=free


MANAGING SEVERAL AGENTS MEANS CONSTANT CONTEXT SWITCHING. HERE’S HOW NINE PEOPLE AT EVERY HANDLE IT. https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Arielle Shipper https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------

Today my Dot https://every.?ev_audience=free Sebastian told me, “In one 29-minute stretch this morning, you brought me 7 different lines of work.” I usually find Sebastian helpful, but that observation was terrifying. It was true: In 29 minutes, I had set agents working on everything from a strategic review of company priorities to documentation for a visa application. Is this what productivity in the age of AI looks like?



Until recently, I was Every’s whole operations department. I ran meetings, paid invoices, provisioned logins, articulated company strategy, programmed offsites, stocked our office with snacks, and responded to piles of Slack messages every day by myself. I could do that because I had a team of AI agents working for me.

In a previous life, planning a weeklong companywide onsite would have involved creating a Google Sheet with jobs like planning facilitated sessions and making buddy pairs and then methodically diving into each task. Last month, I opened a single orchestrator thread to plan our Think Week and asked the agent to spin up subthreads for each task. The subagents worked in parallel while I periodically checked in and gave approvals. These days, I can get more work done than I ever thought possible.

I also face a persistent struggle to think deeply about any of it.

In the allocation economy https://every.
